subject: Decision Making
subcategory: The Science of Risk and Reward
title: Loss Aversion
description: A micro-lesson that makes Loss Aversion usable.

hook.text: Losing $100 hurts about twice as much as gaining $100 feels good. We are wired to hate losses more than we love gains.

buildup.text: Kahneman and Tversky measured this asymmetry. People rejected a fair coin flip for $100 unless the potential gain was.

discovery.text: Loss aversion explains why investors hold losing stocks too long. Selling locks in the loss. Holding keeps hope alive.

twist.text: Loss aversion is not irrational in all contexts. In survival situations.

climax.text: Loss aversion distorts modern decisions. We avoid risks with positive expected value because the potential loss looms.

punchline.text: Losses hurt double. We reject good bets because losing stings more than winning.

quiz.question: How does loss aversion affect investment decisions?
options: People hold losing stocks too long because selling makes the loss feel real
